pages.text: "Sit down to eat!" Mom from the mill put warm bread on the kitchen table. But little brother Mumu took bread in his beak and scurried into the yard. "Running makes it tastier!" His short legs fluttered.
On the straw pile, Mumu tore off another bite. Crumbs dotted every place he had passed. Mom called from the door, "You're still eating!" Mumu paid no attention.
Sparrows flocked down after the crumbs! Chirp, chirp! Startled, Mumu dropped the bread, and the birds pecked the rest. "My bread..." He looked sadly at his empty wings.
Mumu sat on a kitchen chair. Mom tapped the cushion. "Shall we play? This chair has sticky dough hiding inside!" His eyes widened.
A tiny bit of dough in the cushion would hold his bottom firmly. "Then I can't get up?" Mom smiled. "Not until you finish!" Mumu wiggled his bottom. It really felt stuck.
Dad sat opposite. "Bottom on the chair—stay put! One, stick to the cushion! Two, don't move even if sparrows call! Three, empty plate, then hop!" Dad sat firmly first. "Stay put!" Mumu copied him.

Even when a sparrow chirped outside, Mumu didn't move. "Bottom on the chair—stay put!" He held fresh bread in both wings and ate, one bite, two. Only his eyes glanced at the window. His bottom stayed put.
At his empty plate, Mumu puffed out his chest. One tail flick. "The sparrows didn't take a bit!" Mom smiled. "Sit to eat, and all the bread is yours, right?"
Now Mumu knew mealtime rules. "One, stick to the cushion! Two, don't move even if sparrows call! Three, empty plate, then hop!" Next evening, he was already in his chair, wings on the table, waiting.

Mom wrapped both wings around Mumu and stroked his back. "You stayed put even when sparrows called!" Sit to eat, and no bread is taken away. Touching his beak to Mom's cheek, Mumu said, "Bottom on the chair—stay put!"
